workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks 0-8 in order (tasks 1 and 2 are independent of each other; everything else depends on them). Each task is red -> green -> commit on the issue branch; run only the named test file per task, and the full gates (biome, tsc, bun test) once in task 7. Then tester (acceptance 4 E2E on the smoke rig, negative control), reviewer, retro, merger.

implement: legion-worker: the phase contract this plan assumes - workspace binding, jj split for logical paths only, the READY-format PR body from the first push, rebase only when GitHub reports CONFLICTING (base selection in task 0 is not a rebase of a pull request), individual thread disposition, and the smoke proof the implementer's own handoff must carry.
test-driven-development: every task below names the failing test before the code; write it, watch it fail for the stated reason, then make it pass - never the other way round.
verification-before-completion: the handoff claims nothing the implementer has not run - the named test file per task, the three gates in task 7, and the rig log and `legion state` quotes in task 8.

systematic-debugging: a named test that stays red after its step's code is a defect in the step or the plan - trace the durable lane (reducer -> dispatch -> onDequeue -> saveState) before touching an assertion.
test: legion-worker: the E2E section is the real surface (the smoke rig daemon: its boot log, `GET /legion/v1/state`, a live Dispatch status change through the envoy bridge), the exact commands, what was observed, the head SHA, and one negative control; the unit tests are regression locks, never the proof of acceptance 4.
verification-before-completion: quote the rig's daemon.log line and the two `legion state` snapshots from the tester's own run, not from the implementer's handoff.
review: legion-worker: one review per round with every inline finding in one call, thermonuclear-deep-review and thermonuclear-code-quality once at the head, verify CI/Threads/E2E on GitHub directly, `Accepted:`/`Still open:` on every thread you opened, APPROVE only a head that carries no .legion/.
receiving-code-review (for the implementer answering you): findings that change behaviour land in this PR; naming and wording go to the single Fast-follow line.

concerns: LEGION-57 (pull request #1024, 'a released child stays in its parent's tree') rewrites the todo line of reduceIssueUpdated and the whole body of reduceIssueClosed, plus the import lists of reducers.ts, processes.ts and legion-state.ts, and inserts adoptOwnerlessChildTrees between admit() and reconcileAdmission in processes.ts. A textual conflict in reducers.ts is certain whichever lands first. Task 0 chooses the base; the target shapes for both bases are spelled out in task 1 so a conflict-forced resolution is mechanical. The architect agreed this resolution (Envoy message id cdd4ebb499bde3a76d81c08ba2f39e77, 2026-09-13 14:02Z) and recorded it in the spec's New since we talked.

The boot sweep's `unknown issue` rule (spec Errors table) drops any queue entry with no `state.issues` node. Four existing processes.test.ts cases queue keys without seeding issue nodes and would start failing; task 4 names each and seeds `todo` nodes so their intent (tree-status eligibility) is unchanged. Production queue entries always have a node: admit() runs only from a reducer that already required one.

Behavioural consequence to know, not a bug: the controller's periodic queue-reorder pass writes `backlog` then `todo` on a queued issue. After this change the `backlog` write dequeues it and the `todo` write admits it afresh at the back of the queue (the spec's 'a later todo admits it again as a fresh root'). A tester watching `legion state` during a reorder cycle will see a queued issue leave and rejoin.

The production check on LEGION-56 (no new status events across two controller reorder cycles, ~45 min) can only happen after the operator restarts the production daemon on this change; the implementer names it in the PR body's E2E section and, after the merge lands, asks the operator through the architect - the implementer does not restart the production daemon (deployment instructions: only the operator session touches the daemon's checkout).

Every workspace carries a daemon-written empty `.omp/config.yml` that jj auto-snapshots into @ (ProcessManager.writeOmpConfig; not gitignored; absent from main and from #1024). Never let it into a pushed commit: peel logical paths with `jj split -m <message> <paths...>` and point the bookmark at the split-off commit, never at an @ that still holds `.omp/config.yml` (see jjProcedure).
goal: A waiting (queued) issue that Dispatch moves to done, backlog, icebox, or triage leaves the daemon's admission queue and loses its `queued` tree record in the same durable event step as the status change; boot and every resync drop any stale entry already in the queue, logging one line per entry; a later `todo` admits the issue again as a fresh root.
architecture: One exported predicate in legion-state.ts (`isStaleQueuedStatus`, exhaustive over IssueStatus) is the single staleness rule, with a small companion (`staleQueueEntryReason`) that adds the missing-issue-record case for the two sweeps. The pure reducers emit a new `dequeue` effect; the durable lane dispatches it to a new `onDequeue` dep (index.ts wires it to `ProcessManager.dequeue`) before saving, so the queue change and the status change persist together. `ProcessManager.dequeue` splices `admission.queue`, deletes a `queued` tree record, and persists; `reconcileAdmission` runs the same removal over stale entries before its demote/promote loop; `runResync` runs it after the status drift heal through `applyEffects([dequeue, log])`.
globalConstraints: Biome: double quotes, semicolons, ES5 trailing commas, 100-column width. `node:` prefix for builtins, `type` keyword for type-only imports, no barrel files. Strict TypeScript.

One predicate decides staleness: `isStaleQueuedStatus` in legion-state.ts, true for triage/icebox/backlog/done, false for todo/in_progress/testing/needs_review/retro, a `never` default so a new IssueStatus member is a compile error. No second copy of the status list anywhere.
Reducers stay pure: reducers.ts never edits `admission.queue` or `trees`; it emits `{ kind: "dequeue", issue }`. ProcessManager is the only writer of the queue.
No state version bump and no migration: the stored format does not change; the boot sweep runs on every start.
`api/state.ts` and `catchup.ts` are not touched: the controller's queue view is the state, clean once the state is.

Exact log lines. Boot: `[legion] dropped <KEY> from the admission queue at boot: Dispatch status "<status>"` or `[legion] dropped <KEY> from the admission queue at boot: unknown issue` (console.error, like the sibling demote line). Resync: the same text with `at resync` in place of `at boot`, emitted as a `log` effect (the pump prints it as `console.warn("[legion] " + message)`).

The `dequeue` executor is a silent no-op when the issue holds neither a queue entry nor a `queued` tree; it never touches a tree whose status is active, lingering, dead, launch-failed, or closed (only the queue entry goes).

Rebase the pull request only when GitHub reports it CONFLICTING (Sami, 2026-09-11). Task 0's base selection happens before any pull request exists and is not that rebase (architect-agreed, see concerns).
Per task: run only the named test file (`bun test packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/<file>`). Do not run biome, tsc, or the whole suite until task 7.

Commits: jj only. Peel each task's logical paths into its own commit with `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" split -m "<message>" <paths...>`; never `jj describe` an @ that holds `.omp/config.yml`; never `jj abandon`, `jj edit @-`, `jj undo`, or `jj op restore`.

steps.code: - A waiting issue leaves the line with its status. `isStaleQueuedStatus` (`legion-state.ts`) is the one rule -- true for `triage`, `icebox`, `backlog`, `done`; false for `todo` and every daemon-owned status; exhaustive over `IssueStatus` -- and three paths apply it: `reduceIssueUpdated`/`reduceIssueClosed` emit `{kind: "dequeue", issue}` when such a status lands on an issue that holds an `admission.queue` entry or a `queued` tree record (root or child; an active tree still lingers instead), dispatched by the durable lane to `ProcessManager.dequeue` before the save so queue and status persist together; `reconcileAdmission` sweeps the queue at boot before demote/promote; `runResync` sweeps it after `healStatusDrift` through the same effect, logging `dropped <KEY> from the admission queue at resync: <reason>`. `dequeue` splices the queue entry, deletes the tree record only when it is `queued` (active, lingering, dead, launch-failed, and closed records belong to the linger, close, and launch-failure paths), persists, and is a silent no-op when the issue holds neither. tasks.title: Production-like proof on the smoke rig (acceptance 4) and the implement handoff

steps.step: 1. Start the rig in `envoy` mode (Dispatch issue events reach the rig only through the production-Envoy bridge; the shared `LEGSMOKE` project). Follow scripts/smoke/README.md 'Start and stop' exactly; DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN come from ~/.config/opencode/envoy.json.
steps.run: export SMOKE_REPO=sjawhar/legion-smoke SMOKE_PROJECT=sjawhar/24 SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=envoy && secrets ENVOY_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 -- bash -c 'GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET="$ENVOY_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET" exec bash scripts/smoke/up.sh'
steps.expected: `RIG READY`. State lives at /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon/state.json, the log at /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon.log, the API at http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state.

steps.step: 2. Pick a LEGSMOKE issue that is `done` in Dispatch (so the drift heal agrees with the seed) and one that is `backlog` (the negative control later).
steps.run: TOKEN=$(jq -r .dispatch.token ~/.config/opencode/envoy.json); URL=$(jq -r .dispatch.serverUrl ~/.config/opencode/envoy.json); curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$URL/api/v1/issues?project=LEGSMOKE" | jq -r '.[] | select(.status=="done" or .status=="backlog") | "\(.key) \(.status) \(.title)"' | head
steps.expected: At least one `done` key (call it $DONE) and one `backlog` key (call it $PARKED).

steps.step: 3. Stop only the rig daemon you started, back up its state, and seed LEGION-56's shape: $DONE queued at the head with a `queued` tree; also lower the cap to 1 so step 6 can produce a genuinely waiting issue.
steps.run: kill -TERM "$(cat /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon.pid)" && until ! curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done && cp /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon/state.json /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon/state.json.bak && jq --arg k "$DONE" '.issues[$k] = {key: $k, title: "seeded finished issue", status: "done", children: []} | .trees[$k] = {root: $k, generation: 0, status: "queued", launchFailures: 0} | .admission.queue = [$k] + .admission.queue' /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon/state.json.bak > /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon/state.json && sed -i 's/^admission_cap: .*/admission_cap: 1/' /tmp/legion-smoke/legion.yaml && jq '.admission, .trees[$k]' --arg k "$DONE" /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon/state.json
steps.expected: `admission.queue` starts with $DONE; `trees[$DONE].status == "queued"`. Quote this as `legion state` BEFORE (it is the same JSON the API serves).

steps.step: 4. Restart the daemon exactly as up.sh does (same env block, same command) and wait for the API.
steps.run: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && ( env ENVOY_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:14222 ENVOY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:19020 LEGION_DAEMON_PORT=19370 DISPATCH_URL="$URL" DISPATCH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" LEGION_STATE_DIR=/tmp/legion-smoke/daemon XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/legion-smoke/xdg-data XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/legion-smoke/xdg-state bun run packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts start sjawhar/24 --config /tmp/legion-smoke/legion.yaml >>/tmp/legion-smoke/daemon.log 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon.pid ) && until curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done
steps.detail: Ports are the README defaults (NATS 14222, listener 19020, daemon 19370); if you overrode NATS_PORT/ENVOY_PORT/LEGION_DAEMON_PORT for up.sh, use the same values. Re-running `bash scripts/smoke/up.sh` also restarts a dead daemon and reuses the live listener/NATS, and is acceptable instead of this command.

steps.step: 5. Acceptance 4, part one: the boot log line and the clean state.
steps.run: grep -F "dropped $DONE from the admission queue at boot" /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon.log && curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state | jq --arg k "$DONE" '{queue: .admission.queue, active: .admission.active, tree: .trees[$k]}'
steps.expected: Exactly one line `[legion] dropped <DONE> from the admission queue at boot: Dispatch status "done"`; `queue` no longer contains $DONE; `tree` is null; whatever was already active/queued before the seed is unchanged. Quote both as `legion state` AFTER.

steps.step: 6. Acceptance 4, part two: a genuinely waiting issue closed in Dispatch leaves on that one event. With cap 1 and the rig's root active (checkpoint 2), create a fresh LEGSMOKE issue, release it to `todo`, and confirm it queues.
steps.run: NEW=$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST "$URL/api/v1/issues" -d '{"project":"LEGSMOKE","title":"LEGION-79 smoke: waiting issue to close"}' | jq -r .key) && curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PATCH "$URL/api/v1/issues/$NEW" -d '{"status":"todo"}' >/dev/null && sleep 15 && curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state | jq --arg k "$NEW" '{queue: .admission.queue, tree: .trees[$k]}'
steps.expected: `queue` contains $NEW and `tree.status == "queued"` (if `active` is empty because no root is running, first admit another issue so the single slot is taken, or the new issue spawns instead of queueing). Quote as BEFORE.

steps.step: 7. Close it and observe the same durable step remove it.
steps.run: curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PATCH "$URL/api/v1/issues/$NEW" -d '{"status":"done"}' >/dev/null && sleep 15 && curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state | jq --arg k "$NEW" '{queue: .admission.queue, tree: .trees[$k], status: .issues[$k].status}' && grep -c "dropped $NEW" /tmp/legion-smoke/daemon.log
steps.expected: `queue` no longer contains $NEW, `tree` is null, `status` is `done`; the grep count is 0 (the live path is the reducer effect, which logs nothing -- only the sweeps log). Quote as AFTER. If the envoy bridge lags, wait up to a minute and re-read.

steps.step: 8. Negative control (for the tester's E2E line): closing an issue that is not waiting changes nothing in the queue.
steps.run: curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state | jq '.admission' > /tmp/legion-79-before.json && curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PATCH "$URL/api/v1/issues/$PARKED" -d '{"status":"done"}' >/dev/null && sleep 15 && curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19370/legion/v1/state | jq '.admission' | diff /tmp/legion-79-before.json - && echo unchanged && curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X PATCH "$URL/api/v1/issues/$PARKED" -d '{"status":"backlog"}' >/dev/null
steps.expected: `unchanged`; the daemon log has no `dropped $PARKED` line. The last command puts $PARKED back to backlog.

steps.step: 9. Restore the rig config cap (`admission_cap: 4`) and tear down when finished: `bash scripts/smoke/down.sh` (keep SMOKE_REPO/SMOKE_PROJECT exported). Leave $NEW closed; it is a rig-project issue.

steps.run: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && legion handoff write --phase implement --data '{"summary":"...","commits":[...],"smoke":{"bootLogLine":"...","stateBefore":{...},"stateAfter":{...},"liveCloseBefore":{...},"liveCloseAfter":{...},"negativeControl":"unchanged"},"prUrl":"..."}' && test -f "$LEGION_WORKSPACE/.legion/implement.json" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" split -m "implement: record handoff" .legion/implement.json && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" bookmark set legion/LEGION-79 -r @- && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-79 && legion handoff complete --summary '<two sentences>'

reviewerNotes: Exactly one status list: `isStaleQueuedStatus` in legion-state.ts, with a `never` default. Grep for `"icebox"` in the diff: it must appear only there and in tests.
Reducers never touch `admission.queue`/`trees`; the effect is executed only by `ProcessManager.dequeue`, and `dequeue` deletes a tree record only when it is `queued`.
`onDequeue` is awaited in the pump's `dispatch` so a persist failure is fatal; `index.ts` wires it to `processManager.dequeue`.
Boot sweep is before the demote/promote loop and logs the exact spec line; resync sweep is after `healStatusDrift` and goes through `applyEffects` (`dequeue` + `log`).
No state version bump; `api/state.ts` and `catchup.ts` untouched; the four re-seeded processes tests keep their original assertions.
If the PR was rebased over LEGION-57, `reduceIssueClosed` follows the `own`/`result` shape with a single changed initialiser and LEGION-57's child-linger behaviour is preserved.
